links.outcome: Readability instruction-following error and expert preference for readability-controlled versus GPT-4 outputs
links.effect: MedReadCtrl had lower readability instruction-following error than GPT-4 (1.39 vs. 1.59 on ReadMe, p<0.001). Experts preferred MedReadCtrl 71.7% vs. 23.3%, especially at low literacy levels.
links.quote: MedReadCtrl achieves significantly lower readability instruction-following errors than GPT-4 (e.g., 1.39 vs. 1.59 on ReadMe, p<0.001)

unlisted_practices: Readability-controlled instruction tuning of LLMs to adjust output complexity to the target literacy level

screen.reason: Evaluates a readability-controlled instruction framework for tailoring LLM medical text complexity to patient literacy levels, tested via benchmarks and expert evaluation.
